statement.p: Air pressure decreases at a rate of 2 pascals per kilometer in the eastward direction. In addition, the air pressure is decreasing at a constant rate with respect to time everywhere. A ship sailing eastward at 12 km/hour past an island takes barometer readings and records a pressure drop of 70 pascals in 2 hours. Estimate the time rate of change of air pressure on the island. (A pascal is a unit of air pressure.)
Time rate of change of air pressure =

static.solution:
p(x,t) be the air pressure in pascals at x km east of the island at time t hours after the ship passes the island. We want to compute \partial p/\partial t.
Let S(t) be the air pressure on the ship at time t, so that S(t)=p(12 t, t). By the chain rule we have {dS\over dt} = {\partial p\over \partial x}{dx\over dt} + {\partial p\over \partial t}{dt\over dt} = {\partial p\over \partial x}{dx\over dt} + {\partial p\over \partial t}. Since dS/dt \approx (-70 \hbox{ pascal})/(2 \hbox{ hour}) = -35 \mbox{ pascal}/\mbox{hour}, and \partial p/ \partial x = -2\hbox{ pascal/km}, and dx / dt = 12 \hbox{ km/hour}, solving for \partial p / \partial t, we have {\partial p \over \partial t} = -35 \hbox{ pascal/hour} + (2 \hbox{ pascal/km}) (12 \hbox{ km/hour} ) = -11\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut Pa}{\rm\mathstrut hr}}
